Mildly positive but cautious. The Committee highlights strong labor markets and robust household spending, yet underscores persistent weakness in business fixed investment and exports alongside inflation running below target. In line with the natural-rate perspective of Friedman and Phelps, low unemployment without rising inflation suggests no long-run trade-off; New Keynesian evidence of a flat Phillips curve and the centrality of expectations (Galí and Gertler; Woodford) supports holding rates as inflation compensation remains low. The noted weakness in business investment is a meaningful downside risk given the importance of internal finance and credit conditions for capex and inventories (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994), which tend to amplify cyclical slowdowns. Continued T-bill purchases and repo operations to maintain ample reserves should bolster policy transmission and money market stability (consistent with interest-rate implementation frameworks in Woodford, 2003). Net tone: supportive stance amid solid labor data, offset by subdued inflation and soft capex/exports.

Representative line: “Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low,” but “business fixed investment and exports remain weak.”
